# Reproduce the paper

This book corresponds to **manuscript version 16**, with 42 supplementary tables and 25 figures. Primary inference uses the verified reconstructed ROSMAP inputs frozen on 18 October 2026. Additional diagnostics reuse those fits. Website rendering does not execute the experiments.

| Level | Command | What runs |
|---|---|---|
| Saved tables | `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py tables` | Extract and verify checksums |
| All figures | `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py figures` | Rebuild 7 main and 18 supplementary figures |
| Additional diagnostics | `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py diagnostics` | Score groups, equal-budget controls, bootstrap uncertainty and null sensitivities |
| Independent native benchmark | `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py independent-run` | Install archived inference source, generate cohorts, fit both methods and analyze |
| Reconstructed brain inputs | `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py brain-prepare` | Extract verified inputs and the portable workflow |
| Brain native analyses | `python3 reproduction/reproduce.py brain-run` | Install archived source and execute parts 00–07 |

Run commands from the repository root. `--out work/another-run` chooses a separate output directory. Saved tables are never silently overwritten when they differ from the release archive. Native fit caches are validated before reuse.

## Install requirements

The package installation is described [here](install.qmd). Figure creation also needs Python's `reportlab` and `pypdfium2`:

```bash
python3 -m venv work/figure-env
work/figure-env/bin/python -m pip install reportlab pypdfium2
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py figures --out work/figure-rebuild --python work/figure-env/bin/python
```

The [dependency lock and restore instructions](https://github.com/kkang7/CDSeq2/tree/main/reproduction/environment) record the benchmark environment. Native runs require the benchmark dependencies, R 4.6.1 for exact environment matching, and a compilation toolchain. Restore into an isolated library. The driver installs the archived **0.0.0.9000** inference source into `work/benchmark-library`; package release **0.1.0** adds reporting and tests while preserving the benchmark inference/scoring functions. Current package and exact benchmark versions serve different purposes and are recorded explicitly.

## Independent cohorts

```bash
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py independent-prepare
Rscript tools/install_dependencies.R benchmark
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py independent-run --workers 4
```

See the [benchmark chapter](independent-eqtl.qmd) for the frozen design and resource scope. The complete native benchmark is a substantial computation. The compact archive contains parameters, reference, scorer, haplotypes, source and completed results, without native-fit caches. Exact environment checks fail on incompatible dependencies rather than silently combining versions.

## Reconstructed brain analyses

```bash
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py brain-prepare
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py brain-run
```

The input archive includes the four reconstructed study inputs, frozen donor/gene/nucleus selections and a portable configuration. These inputs reproduced source aggregation exactly and generated the v15/v16 results. They differ from the historical input version used by v14. The [brain chapter](brain-benchmarks.qmd) describes source verification against downloaded ROSMAP files and the historical reconstruction audit.

## Additional diagnostics

```bash
python3 reproduction/reproduce.py diagnostics --out work/diagnostic-check
```

This regenerates Tables S36–S42, Figure 7 and Figures S16–S18 from compact verified inputs and saved independent-cohort test results, then independently checks counts, selection membership, metrics and null sensitivity. It runs no new native inference and changes no primary analysis. Full RDS input provenance and the exact scorer are in [downloads](data.qmd).

The [validation record](../downloads/book_validation.txt) distinguishes local completed checks from GitHub/Linux checks awaiting execution. A successful website build alone does not verify statistical computations.
